Assigning ASVs with DADA2

Roger Calvas

2026-10-28

Setear variables de ambientes

Semilla y threads

# Set the seed for reproducibility
set.seed(9473)

# Let's make a parameter to set the number of threads 
n_threads = 20

Tiempo de inicio

# What time did we start running this script? 
start_time <- Sys.time()

Load Packages

#install.packages("janitor")
# Efficient package loading with pacman 
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, devtools, dada2, 
               patchwork, DT, phyloseq, janitor, install = FALSE)

Objetivos del archivo:

  1. Inferir el modelo de error de DADA2 tanto en las R1 como R2
  2. Asignar ASVs usando el modelo de error tanto en R1 como R2
  3. Empalmar las secuencias para generar una tabla de ASVs continua
  4. Crear el primer draft de la tabla de recuento de ASVs
  5. Chequear estadistica de ASVs
  6. Quitar quimeras
  7. Asignar taxonomia con UNITE
  8. Guardar los archivos relevantes: asv_table, asvs_fasta, tax_table, y sample_data

Input

  1. Fastq filtrados de 01_QC_DADA2.Rmd
  2. Vector de sample_names

Output

  1. Tabla de conteo de asvs: asv_table (Con y sin nombre de secuencia)
  2. Tabla de taxonomia asignada tax_table
  3. Un objeto phyloseq raw (S4 object): raw_physeq.RData

Cargar datos

Cargar fastqs

# Place filtered seq files into a variable 
filtered_fastqs_path <- "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs"

# Intuition check:
filtered_fastqs_path
## [1] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs"
# Create Forward vector 
filtered_forward_reads <- 
  list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "R1_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)
# Check 
filtered_forward_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-004_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-006_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [3] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-007_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [4] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-011_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [5] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-018_R1_filtered.fastq.gz"
# Reverse vector 
filtered_reverse_reads <- 
    list.files(filtered_fastqs_path, pattern = "R2_filtered.fastq.gz",
             full.names = TRUE)

# Check 
filtered_reverse_reads[1:5]
## [1] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-004_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [2] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-006_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"
## [3] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-007_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"

## [5] "data/its/01_DADA2/filtered_fastqs/ANF-018_R2_filtered.fastq.gz"

Nombres de muestras

# Create vector of sample names from the filenames
sample_names <- sapply(strsplit(basename(filtered_forward_reads), "_"), `[`, 1) 

# Intuition Check 
head(sample_names)
## [1] "ANF-004" "ANF-006" "ANF-007" "ANF-011" "ANF-018" "ANF-021"

Prediccion de errores

Funcion de estimacion para bins

# Declarar los bins del secuenciador
binnedQs <- c(2, 11, 25, 37)

# Crear la funcion en base a los bins
binnedErrFun <- makeBinnedQualErrfun(binnedQs)

Calcular los errores

# Forward Reads con binned err fun
error_forward_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_forward_reads, multithread = n_threads, nbases = 3e8, errorEstimationFunction = binnedErrFun)
## 301323930 total bases in 1335234 reads from 23 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# clase
saveRDS(error_forward_reads, file = "data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/error_forward_reads.rds")
# Forward Error Plot 
forward_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_forward_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Forward Reads: Error Model")

# Reverse Reads con binned err fun
error_reverse_reads <- 
  learnErrors(filtered_reverse_reads, multithread = n_threads, nbases = 3e8, errorEstimationFunction = binnedErrFun)
## 308626572 total bases in 1384506 reads from 24 samples will be used for learning the error rates.
# clase
saveRDS(error_reverse_reads, file = "data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/error_reverse_reads.rds")
# Reverse Error Plot 
reverse_error_plot <- 
  plotErrors(error_reverse_reads, nominalQ = TRUE) + 
  labs(title = "Reverse Reads: Error Model")

# Look at the plots together 
forward_error_plot + reverse_error_plot

Preguntas 1: La secuencia tenia calidades binned y como se ajusto la curva de error?

[La secuencia tenia bins en: ‘2, 11, 25, 37’ y la curva de error se ajusto mejor al aplicar el modelo para secuenciadores de bins]

Inferir e inspeccionar ASVs

Inferir ASVs

# Infer ASVs on the forward sequences
dada_forward <- 
  dada(filtered_forward_reads, 
       err = error_forward_reads,
       multithread = n_threads)

# Inspect the distribution of sequence lengths of all ASVs in data set 
plot_ASVLength_raw <- 
  data.frame(Seq_Length = nchar(getSequences(raw_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Seq_Length )) + 
  geom_histogram() + 
  # include the x-axis scales
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, maxLength_ASV + 5)) + 
  labs(y = "Number of ASVs", x = "Raw ASV Length (bps)")

Remover Chimeras

# Remove the chimeras in the raw ASV table
noChimeras_ASV_table <- 
  removeBimeraDenovo(raw_ASV_table, 
                     method="consensus", 
                     multithread = n_threads, 
                     verbose=TRUE)
## Identified 92 bimeras out of 5496 input sequences.
# Clase 
saveRDS(noChimeras_ASV_table, file = "data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/noChimeras_ASV_table.rds")
# Check the dimensions
dim(noChimeras_ASV_table)
## [1]   34 5404
# Chimera removal compared to raw  
percRetained_chimerasRaw <-sum(noChimeras_ASV_table)/sum(raw_ASV_table)

# Plot it 
plot_ASVLength_NoChimeras <- 
  data.frame(Seq_Length_NoChim = nchar(getSequences(noChimeras_ASV_table))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Seq_Length_NoChim )) + 
  geom_histogram()+ 
  # include the x-axis scales
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, maxLength_ASV + 5)) + 
  labs(y = "Number of ASVs \n (Post-Chimera Removal)", 
       x = "ASV Length (bps)")

Track the read counts

# A little function to identify number seqs 
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))

# Make the table to track the seqs 
track <- cbind(sapply(dada_forward, getN),
               sapply(dada_reverse, getN),
               sapply(merged_ASVs, getN),
               rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Update column names to be more informative (most are missing at the moment!)
colnames(track) <- c("denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")

# Generate a dataframe to track the reads through our DADA2 pipeline
track_counts_df <- 
  track %>%
  # make it a dataframe
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "sample_names")

# Now let's add a column for the number of ASVs
# First, intuition check that the samples match 
stopifnot(track_counts_df$sample_names == row.names(noChimeras_ASV_table))

# Now, let's add a new column with the number of ASVs
track_counts_df <- 
  track_counts_df %>%
  mutate(num_ASVs = rowSums(noChimeras_ASV_table > 1))

# Visualize it in table format 
DT::datatable(track_counts_df)
saveRDS(track_counts_df, file = "data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/track_counts_df.rds")

# Plot it!
track_counts_df %>%
  pivot_longer(denoisedF:nochim, names_to = "read_type", values_to = "num_reads") %>%
  mutate(read_type = fct_relevel(read_type, "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nochim")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = read_type, y = num_reads, fill = read_type)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = sample_names), color = "grey") + 
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, alpha = 0.8) + 
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Spectral") + 
  labs(x = "Filtering Step", y = "Number of Sequences") + 
  theme_bw()

Preguntas 3: Que proporcion de los ASVs se mantuvo despues de quitar quimeras? Hay algun detalle adicional en relacion a la retencion de muestras que puedas mencionar?

[La mayoria de ASVs se retuvieron despues de eliminar quimeras y la mayoria de las muestras tienen alrededor de 50k reads, adicional no parece haber ninguna relacion entre la profundidad de secuenciamiento y el numero de ASVs, algo que da mas seguridad al analisis]

ASV_seqs[1:5]

## [4] "AAAGTGCGATAACTAGTGTGAATTGCATATTCAGTGAATCATCGAGTCTTTGAACGCAACTTGCGCTCCTTGGTATTCCATGGAGCACGCCTGTTTCAGTATCAAAACAAACCCTCTACCGCTCTTCTGCTCTTTTTGTGGACGGAGACAGTAGGAACATTGGAAGTCTCCCGGCGAGTTTACTCAGCGGGGAAGCCTCTGAAATTTATTTAGGCTTGAGCATGGTTCAATTATGCCGAAACTTTTTTTTTAATATAAAGAAAAAGTTCAAGCGACCGAGCCGCCGCAAGAGCCTCCCAAATAAAATATTTTTTAAATTTGATCTGAAATCAGGCGGGATTACCCGCTGAACTTAA"                  
## [5] "GTGGTTCCGGGTCTGTTGCATAAGTATAGCAATCGCGCCCTGTTACTGGTGAAAGGCGGGTGTGCGGTGAATTGCCGCTACTGTTTCCGCCGTCATTTCCCGTATCAGGACAACCAGGGAAATAAGGCCAACTGGGTTCAGGCGCTGGATTATATCCGCACATGTCCCGAACTCGATGAAATTATTTTCTCTGGCGGCGATCCGCTGATGGCGAAAGATCACGAACTCGACTGGCTGATCAGTGAACTGGAAGGGATCCCGCACATAAAACGTCTGCGGATCCACACCCGTTTACCCGTTGTGATCCCGGCACGTATTACTGATACGCTCTGCCAGCGCCTTGAACAATCACGCCTGCAGGTGCTGATGGTTAC"
# How many ASVs? 
num_ASVs <- dim(final_ASV_table_withSeqs)[1] # select the number of rows
num_ASVs 
## [1] 5404
# which is where we will place the new operational ASV names 
ASV_headers <- vector(num_ASVs, mode = "character")

# Let's mae sure we have an empty vector!
ASV_headers[1:5]
## [1] "" "" "" "" ""
length(ASV_headers) # looks good! 
## [1] 5404
# Ahora creemos un vector con ASVs numerados usando un loop
for (i in 1:num_ASVs) {
  # Add leading zero to ASV name so they print in correct order.
  ASV_number <- sprintf("%04d", i)
  # Now, rename each spot in the ASV header vector as we loop through the for loop
  ASV_headers[i] <- paste(">ASV", ASV_number, sep = "_")
}

# Intuition check
ASV_headers[1:5]
## [1] ">ASV_0001" ">ASV_0002" ">ASV_0003" ">ASV_0004" ">ASV_0005"
# Create a new ASV table, which will have the ASV numbers as names 
#View(noChimeras_ASV_table) # To view the table
final_ASV_table <- final_ASV_table_withSeqs
glimpse(final_ASV_table)
##  int [1:5404, 1:34] 0 3656 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 0 ...
##  - attr(*, "dimnames")=List of 2
##   ..$ : chr [1:5404] "GAAACGCGATATGTAATGTGAATTGCAGAATTCAGTGAATCATCGAATCTTTGAACGCACATGGCGCCTTCCAGTATCCTGGGAGGCATGCCTGTCCGAGCGTCGTTTCAA"| __truncated__ "GAAATGCGATAAGTAATGTGAATTGCAGAATTCAGTGAATCATCGAATCTTTGAACGCACATTGCGCCCCCTGGTATTCCGGGGGGCATGCCTGTTCGAGCGTCATTTCAC"| __truncated__ "GAAATGCGATAAGTAATGTGAATTGCAGAATTCAGTGAATCATCGAATCTTTGAACGCACCTTGCGCTCCATGGTATTCCGTGGAGCATGCCTGTTTGAGTGTCATGAATA"| __truncated__ "AAAGTGCGATAACTAGTGTGAATTGCATATTCAGTGAATCATCGAGTCTTTGAACGCAACTTGCGCTCCTTGGTATTCCATGGAGCACGCCTGTTTCAGTATCAAAACAAA"| __truncated__ ...
##   ..$ : chr [1:34] "ANF-004" "ANF-006" "ANF-007" "ANF-011" ...
## Replace the ASV seqs with the ASV numbers 
row.names(final_ASV_table) <- sub(">", "", ASV_headers)
final_ASV_table[1:5, 1:5]

Escribir tablas de ASVs

write.table(final_ASV_table_withSeqs, 
            file = "data/its/02_Assign_ASVs/ASV_table_withSeqNames.tsv", 
            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)

# 2. Write count table with ASV numbered names (e.g. ASV_1, ASV_2, etc)
write.table(final_ASV_table,

            sep = "\t", quote = FALSE, col.names = NA)

2. Taxonomy Table

Formatear la tabla

# Inspect the taxonomy table
dim(taxa_train) # ASVs are in rows and Kingdom, Phylum, etc in Columns

colnames(taxa_train) # Column names are Linnean Taxonomy

head(rownames(taxa_train), n = 2) # ASV names are rownames 
## [1] "GAAACGCGATATGTAATGTGAATTGCAGAATTCAGTGAATCATCGAATCTTTGAACGCACATGGCGCCTTCCAGTATCCTGGGAGGCATGCCTGTCCGAGCGTCGTTTCAACCCTCGAGCCCCTGTGGCCCGGCGTTGGGGATCTGCCACGGCAGGCCCCTAAAACCAGTGGCGGACCCGAAGGGCCCTCTCCTTTGCGCAGTAGCATTCGCCTCGCATCGGGAGTCCTCGGCGTCCTGCCTCTAAACCCCCCACAAGCCCGCCTCGGCGGCACCAAGGTTGACCTCGGATCAGGTAGGAATACCCGCTGAACTTAA"

class(taxa_train) # Character matrix
## [1] "matrix" "array"
##### Prepare tax table 
# 1. Add the ASV sequences from the rownames to a column 
new_tax_table <- 
  taxa_train%>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rownames_to_column(var = "ASVseqs") 

# Intuition check 
glimpse(new_tax_table)

### Final prep of tax table. Add new column with ASV names 
ASV_tax_table <- 
  new_tax_table %>%
  # add rownames from count table for phyloseq handoff
  mutate(ASV = rownames(final_ASV_table)) %>%
  # Reorder the columns
  dplyr::select(Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species, ASV, ASVseqs)

# Assign the rownames, which is required by phyloseq
rownames(ASV_tax_table) <- ASV_tax_table$ASV
